The distribution guidance is a reference point, not a quota. If this group is different, that's fine, as long as the evidence supports it and we write down why.
Please stick to evidence about the work. We don't discuss health, family situations, leave, age, nationality, visa status or personal life. If that comes up, I'll pause the discussion.
Before we close, I'll read back every change and its reason, and the Dept Head will confirm the final outcomes.
What specific results did this person deliver against their goals, and how do we know?
items.detail: Ask for artifacts: tape-out milestones, coverage numbers, bugs found or escaped, customer outcomes. Push back on adjectives.

items.text: How does this compare with the written expectations for the level, rather than with others on the team?
Would we rate the same evidence the same way if it came from a different team or site?
items.detail: Tests leniency and severity differences between managers and between sites such as Hsinchu, Bengaluru, Munich, Haifa, Austin and San Jose.

items.text: Does this rating reflect the whole period, or mostly the last few weeks?
Is this work visible or invisible? Are we under-crediting verification, DFT, infrastructure or support work compared with architecture and customer escalations?
For a proposed 1 or 2: was the gap raised earlier in the year, with dated check-ins and support offered?
items.detail: If not, the rating may still be right, but the next step is documented coaching, not a PIP.

items.text: For a promotion: is the person already working at the next level consistently, against the published criteria, and is there a business need?
items.detail: Check H-1B holders with Immigration before the effective date; an amended petition and a new I-129 Part 6 determination may be needed.

items.text: Is anything other than performance shaping this discussion, such as schedule flexibility, leave, remote status, accent or communication style?

sections.title: Bias checks
sections.intro: The facilitator raises these in the moment, neutrally, and records only the outcome.

items.text: Recency: the evidence covers the whole period, not just the last project.
Halo and horns: one strong or weak area is not driving every competency rating.
Similarity and affinity: 'reminds me of myself', same school or same former employer.
Visibility and proximity: remote, part-time, flexible-schedule and other-site employees are judged on output, not face time.
Leave and caregiving: time on protected leave, reserve duty or sick leave is excluded, and 'commitment' is not inferred from leave or flexible hours.
Language and style: accent, English fluency or a quiet style in meetings are not treated as performance unless communication is a documented role requirement with examples.
Rater effects: managers who rate everyone high or everyone low are corrected to the evidence, not to the average.
Group outcomes: at the end, review the analytics pack for any group with materially lower ratings; each flagged gap is explained by evidence or escalated to HR Analytics and Legal.
Guidance: about 15-20% in the top two ratings and 5-10% below expectations, across a population large enough to be meaningful (roughly 25+). It is a sanity check, not a quota.
Where the group is well outside the guidance, what evidence explains it?
items.detail: E.g., a team that achieved first-pass silicon success, or a new team still ramping. Record the rationale.

items.text: No rating is changed only to fit the guidance; every change cites evidence.
Compare distributions across managers, sites and job families in the same org, and investigate outliers.
Forced distribution needs works council agreement in Germany, and in small teams a forced curve creates arbitrary low ratings and litigation exhibits.

For each change, the HRBP records the employee, proposed rating, calibrated rating, evidence-based reason and decision owner. No verbatim debate, personality opinions or references to protected characteristics.
Notes are stored in the restricted Darwinbox calibration folder under the retention schedule (at least 5 years for Israel; 4 years for California ADS records).
Read back every change at the end and have the Dept Head confirm it.
Calibration notes are discoverable in litigation and can fall within access requests (GDPR, PIPL, DPDP, CCPA). Write only what you would be comfortable having the employee and a judge read.
Participants must not share other employees' ratings, the discussion or comparisons after the session; breaches are handled under the Code of Conduct.
Managers update evidence or ratings in Darwinbox within 2 business days.
HR Analytics reruns the adverse-impact analysis on calibrated ratings, and flagged gaps are reviewed with Legal under privilege before the lock.
Legal/ER signs off below-expectations ratings in the high-risk population before release.
The Dept Head approves; People Ops locks ratings and reconciles record counts to the comp planning tool (SOX control).
HRBP prepares managers for difficult conversations and routes below-expectations ratings to documented coaching or PD-03. A PIP is never launched in the review meeting.
Promotion outcomes go to Total Rewards for pay and equity under PD-04, after the Colorado internal-posting, German §99 consent and H-1B amendment checks are complete.

notes: Calibrate the bottom first: below-expectations ratings carry the most legal risk and feed PIPs and RIF selection.
Use a guidance distribution, not forced ranking. Deviations are fine when they are documented with evidence.
Protected characteristics, leave and visa status are never discussed. The analytics pack covers group outcomes so the room doesn't have to.
Keep the room small and informed: managers who know the work, the Dept Head and the HRBP.
Write notes as if they will be read in court. They may be, and employees can request them in several jurisdictions.
Promotion calibration uses the same evidence standard and the published criteria; no one promises dates or equity in the room.
In multi-country orgs, let non-US managers present in their working language and respect local prerequisites (works council agreement, China democratic procedure, Vietnam task-completion criteria).

countryNotes.us: Calibration outcomes are central evidence in discrimination claims. Run adverse-impact analysis under privilege, including by visa status given EEOC, DOJ IER and DOL scrutiny, and keep promotion criteria open to all.
countryNotes.us-ca: Have Legal review below-expectations ratings within 90 days of protected activity. Algorithmic calibration aids are ADS under CRD rules (keep records 4 years), and CCPA ADMT duties start 1 Jan 2027.
countryNotes.us-co: Check outcomes across all CADA classes, including marital status and gender expression. Promotions are usually 'job opportunities' that must be posted to all Colorado employees, with a post-selection notice within 30 days.
countryNotes.us-nc: No state calibration or posting rules. A promotion is valid new consideration for a non-compete signed by a current employee.
countryNotes.us-tx: No Texas calibration or promotion-posting rules. Document the purpose and safeguards of any AI-assisted tools in case of an AG civil investigative demand under TRAIGA.
countryNotes.us-wa: EPOA guarantees equal career-advancement opportunity, so calibration and promotion outcomes are discoverable, and employees offered an internal promotion can request its pay range.
countryNotes.ca: Calibration notes can be produced in wrongful-dismissal and human rights proceedings. Any electronic data used in Ontario ratings must be disclosed in the e-monitoring policy.
countryNotes.de: Calibration procedures and any forced distribution need a works council agreement (§94 BetrVG). Moving someone into a new pay group needs council consent above 20 employees (§99), and the council can require internal posting (§93).
countryNotes.il: Keep sessions reserve-duty neutral and gender-equal, and keep calibration records at least 5 years given the discrimination limitation period.
countryNotes.in: Use aggregated, de-identified analytics under the DPDP Act, and make sure rating-linked pay is gender-neutral (Code on Wages s.3). A promotion into a managerial role can change 'worker' status, so record the duties change.
countryNotes.tw: Keep up to 10 sick days a year and protected leave out of the discussion. A promotion to manager does not remove overtime coverage in Taiwan.
countryNotes.cn: The rating scale and any distribution guidance must have been adopted through democratic procedure and publicized. Use aggregated analytics and keep individual data in China unless transfer rules are met.
countryNotes.vn: Calibrate against the published task-completion criteria. Record promotions in a contract annex with the new salary, which becomes the SI contribution base.
